nodes.description:
There is no treatment that restores ciliary function. Management is the supportive care used across primary ciliary dyskinesia: airway clearance, prompt treatment of respiratory infections, and macrolide prophylaxis, for which a randomized trial of azithromycin in PCD reduced pulmonary exacerbations. Nothing in it is specific to DNAH5.
Curated as a single scoping entry rather than an itemised regimen, because no trial has enrolled by genotype and the umbrella Primary_Ciliary_Dyskinesia entry holds the detailed management block. What is DNAH5-specific is prognostic: lung function is on average better than in the CCDC39/CCDC40 class, which is curated on the bronchiectasis phenotype.

nodes.description: Dnah5-deficient mice have immotile efferent duct cilia lacking outer dynein arms, sperm accumulation in the efferent ducts, and normal sperm ultrastructure and motility, matching the oligozoospermia with normal motility seen in patients.

Sperm flagella do not depend on DNAH5, so sperm motility is normal. Motile cilia of the efferent ducts do depend on it; when they are immotile, sperm accumulate in the ducts and the ejaculate sperm count falls.

nodes.description: An insertional mutation in mouse Dnah5 reproduces the core PCD features: loss of outer dynein arms, immotile cilia, situs inversus and respiratory infection. The mice also develop hydrocephalus and die perinatally, which is far more severe than the human disease.
Common in DNAH5 disease, and more common when both alleles are loss-of-function than when one may retain residual function.
